$comment: Every language fog-docs is translated into. Read by scripts/translate.mjs
(which files to produce, which glossary to pull, what banner to inject) and
by quartz/scripts/rtd-build.mjs (which Quartz UI locale to build with).
'code' is Read the Docs' language code -- it is simultaneously the RTD
project's Language setting, the URL prefix RTD serves the site under
(docs.fogproject.org/<code>/latest/), the value RTD passes to the build as
$READTHEDOCS_LANGUAGE, and the directory name under translations/. Those are
the same string on purpose: it means adding a language is one entry here
plus one RTD project, with nothing to keep in sync between them.
'quartzLocale' is the UI-chrome locale Quartz ships in quartz/quartz/i18n/
locales/. It only translates Quartz's own furniture (search placeholder,
'Table of Contents', graph controls) -- page content comes from the
translations/<code>/ tree. Every locale listed here has a file there; check
before adding a language, since a missing locale silently falls back to
English chrome around translated content.
'gettextLocale' names this language's catalog in the fogproject repo
(packages/web/management/languages/<gettextLocale>/LC_MESSAGES/messages.po).
Those are human translations of the actual web UI strings, used as a
terminology glossary so the docs call a button what the reader's screen
calls it. Set to null for a language the web UI has no catalog for -- the
translation still runs, just without pinned terminology.
'banner' is the machine-translation warning prepended to every translated
page. '{url}' is replaced with the English original's URL. It is injected by
code rather than asked of the model so it is always exactly right.

banner.title: Traduction automatique
banner.body: Cette page a été traduite automatiquement et peut contenir des erreurs. En cas de doute, reportez-vous à [la version anglaise]({url}).
